claim: For the two-qubit XXZ Hamiltonian in a uniform field \(B\) and field inhomogeneity \(b\) studied by Zhang and Li, \[H=\frac12\!\left[J(\sigma_x\otimes\sigma_x+\sigma_y\otimes\sigma_y)+J_z\sigma_z\otimes\sigma_z+(B+b)\sigma_z\otimes I+(B-b)I\otimes\sigma_z\right],\]assume \(J>0\), \(J_z\ge0\), \(T>0\), and put \(\eta=\sqrt{J^2+b^2}\). The exact Gibbs-state concurrence is \[C(T,b)=\frac{2}{Z}\left[e^{J_z/(2T)}\frac{J}{\eta}\sinh(\eta/T)-e^{-J_z/(2T)}\right]_+,\]where \(Z=2e^{-J_z/(2T)}\cosh(B/T)+2e^{J_z/(2T)}\cosh(\eta/T)\). Therefore \(C(T,b)>0\) if and only if \[\frac{J}{\eta}\sinh(\eta/T)>e^{-J_z/T}.\]Because \(\sinh x/x\) is strictly increasing for \(x>0\), increasing \(|b|\) can never destroy existing concurrence. If \(\sinh(J/T)>e^{-J_z/T}\), then \(C(T,b)>0\) for every finite \(b\); if equality holds, only \(b=0\) is at threshold; and if \(\sinh(J/T)<e^{-J_z/T}\), there is one lower activation threshold \(b_*>0\), determined by \[\frac{J}{\sqrt{J^2+b_*^2}}\sinh\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{J^2+b_*^2}}{T}\right)=e^{-J_z/T},\]with \(C=0\) for \(|b|\le b_*\) and \(C>0\) for \(|b|>b_*\). Whenever it exists, \(b_*\) strictly decreases with \(J_z\). Moreover, for fixed \(J,J_z,B,T\), \[\lim_{|b|\to\infty}\frac{|b|}{J}C(T,b)=1,\]so \(C(T,b)\sim J/|b|\). Thus the finite upper critical inhomogeneity reported in the source does not exist; inhomogeneity can instead activate entanglement and leaves an algebraic positive tail.

integrity.computational_dependence: none for the theorem; direct matrix replay is supplementary
integrity.novelty_scope: Correction of the claimed finite upper inhomogeneity cutoff, exact one-threshold activation topology, Jz-dependence of the activation threshold, and universal reciprocal concurrence tail.
integrity.ownership_basis: The mathematically indexed close XXZ inhomogeneous-field treatment DOI:10.1142/S0217979206034583 has primary MSC 81P68.
integrity.prior_work_preserved: The Gibbs state and concurrence formula are credited to Zhang and Li; the isotropic inhomogeneous-field activation phenomenon is credited to Asoudeh and Karimipour.

scientific_limitations: The theorem assumes J>0 and Jz>=0 and concerns concurrence positivity, not monotonicity of its magnitude.
A closely related 2006 XXZ inhomogeneous-field article could not be fully inspected and is retained as the principal originality risk.
The reciprocal large-inhomogeneity tail is a fixed-parameter asymptotic.
The direct 2005 physics source lacks an accessible MSC record; primary ownership is supported by the close mathematically indexed XXZ treatment with primary MSC 81P68.
title: No finite inhomogeneity cutoff for thermal entanglement in the XXZ dimer
